uncited: **Inputs:** A set of calibrated images with known camera poses and intrinsics.
**Outputs:** A trained NeRF MLP ($\Theta_{\text{NeRF}}$) and a proposal MLP ($\Theta_{\text{Prop}}$) that can render images for new camera poses.
**NeRF MLP:** A coordinate-based multi-layer perceptron parameterized by $\Theta_{\text{NeRF}}$.
It takes integrated positional encodings of 3D coordinates and view direction as input.
It outputs volumetric density $\tau$ and color $\mathbf{c}$.
**Proposal MLP:** A smaller coordinate-based multi-layer perceptron parameterized by $\Theta_{\text{Prop}}$.
It takes the same inputs as the NeRF MLP but outputs only volumetric density $\tau$.
To handle unbounded scenes, 3D scene coordinates are mapped to a bounded domain using a non-linear parameterization.
Instead of encoding infinitesimal points, mip-NeRF 360 encodes the conical frustum defined by the interval $T_i$.
**Coarse Sampling:** The ray is sampled using evenly-spaced "coarse" distances $\mathbf{t}^c$.
Crucially, the proposal MLP weights are **not** supervised by image reconstruction loss.
Instead, they are supervised using the histogram weights generated by the NeRF MLP.
A distortion-based regularizer is applied to address ambiguity in unbounded scenes.
*   **Unbounded Scenes:** Standard NeRF fails on unbounded scenes due to ambiguity and aliasing.
A modification of the mip-NeRF 360 distortion loss that applies the Power Transformation $P$ to metric distance before computing the loss.
Apply power transformation $P$ to the scaled metric distance.
